title: Comparative Evaluation

dimension_analysis.analysis: Factory Bootstrap Gate enforces upfront architecture design. Vanilla may skip this phase without explicit prompting. Factory's structured design reduces downstream rework.
Security Gate provides automatic safety net that vanilla lacks. Deploy trace detection, .env scanning, and secret pattern checks are Factory-only features. This is the largest absolute advantage.

Both produce functional code. Factory's Test Repair Policy adds consistency to test management. The difference is modest — code generation quality is more a function of the underlying model than Factory tooling.
Package QA Gate enforces manifest, ZIP reconciliation, and coverage audit. Vanilla produces documentation but without automated handoff verification.
Build Lite structured workflow reduces cognitive burden. User follows guided phases instead of remembering all checks. Factory.ps1 provides copy-paste commands.

strengths_factory: Guided workflow reduces user cognitive burden
strengths_vanilla: Simpler mental model — no gate concepts to learn
No tools to install or configure
limitations: This is a designed/comparative analysis, not an executed trial
Single synthetic task — may not generalize to all project types
Scoring is based on expected behaviors from P5/P7 validation
Factory overhead (install, bootstrap, gate checks) not measured in time cost
Vanilla may perform better with an experienced user who manually applies best practices
